tagline: Leading producer of factory-built homes with integrated financial services and insurance operations
hero_kpi_rationale: Backlog is the primary indicator of future demand in the factory-built housing sector, reflecting short-term visibility into sales and production.

kpis.name: Backlog
kpis.explanation: Value of orders not yet produced but confirmed, providing visibility into future sales.
kpis.description: Backlog stood at $197 million as of March 29, 2025, an increase of $6 million compared to the prior year.

kpis.name: Total net revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales generated by the company during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: Consolidated net revenue reached $2,015.5 million for fiscal 2025, an increase of 12.3% ($220.7 million) compared to $1,794.8 million in fiscal 2024.
kpis.signal: Robust growth driven by home sales

kpis.name: Factory-built housing revenue
kpis.explanation: Sales of factory-built homes, the company's core business segment.
kpis.description: Factory-built housing revenue reached $1,933.1 million in 2025, an increase of $216.5 million or 12.6% compared to $1,716.6 million in 2024.

kpis.name: Homes sold
kpis.explanation: Total number of factory-built homes sold during the fiscal year.
kpis.description: 19,753 homes were sold in 2025, compared to 16,928 in 2024, representing an increase of 2,825 units or 16.7%.

kpis.name: Gross profit
kpis.explanation: Consolidated gross profit, the difference between revenue and cost of goods sold.
kpis.description: Consolidated gross profit amounted to $465.6 million in 2025, up $38.7 million or 9.1% from $426.9 million in 2024.
kpis.signal: Gross profit growth lagging behind revenue growth

kpis.name: Consolidated gross margin
kpis.explanation: Gross margin as a percentage of consolidated net revenue.
kpis.description: Consolidated gross margin reached 23.1% in 2025, down 0.7 percentage points from 23.8% in 2024.

kpis.name: Housing gross margin
kpis.explanation: Gross margin of the factory-built housing segment.
kpis.description: Factory-built housing gross margin was 22.9% in 2025, down 0.3 percentage points from 23.2% in 2024.
kpis.signal: Slight margin compression in core segment

kpis.name: Financial services revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the financial services segment, including insurance and financing.
kpis.description: Financial services revenue amounted to $82.3 million in 2025, up $4.2 million or 5.3% from $78.2 million in 2024.
kpis.signal: Moderate growth in financial services segment

kpis.name: R&D investments
kpis.description: No mention of distinct R&D investments in the factory-built housing sector.
kpis.signal: Not applicable to the factory-built housing sector

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending on physical assets such as factories or equipment.
kpis.description: Capital expenditures were not detailed in the provided excerpts.

kpis.name: Total headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Total headcount is not indicated in the provided excerpts.

kpis.name: Backlog
kpis.explanation: Value of orders pending production, a key indicator of future demand.
kpis.description: Backlog reached $197 million in 2025, compared to $191 million in 2024, reflecting stable demand.

kpis.name: Revenue growth
kpis.explanation: Increase in consolidated net revenue reflecting strong demand for factory-built homes.
kpis.description: Net revenue reached $2,015.5 million in 2025, up 12.3% from $1,794.8 million in 2024.
kpis.signal: Robust growth driven by high volumes

kpis.name: Volume growth
kpis.explanation: Increase in the number of homes sold, reflecting higher demand.
kpis.description: 19,753 homes sold in 2025 versus 16,928 in 2024, an increase of 2,825 units.

risks.title: Cyber incidents potentially disrupting operations
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly mentioned at the top of the operational risk factors. Although the company states no material impact has occurred, it acknowledges that IT failures or cyber incidents could harm the business. The language is preventive but serious, with dedicated governance reinforcing the perceived severity.

risks.title: Credit risks in customer financing
risks.score_rationale: The text explicitly mentions exposure to risks related to the solvency of dealers, land owners, and financing partners. The company directly finances commercial loans, creating default risk. This risk is recurring and intensified by the structure of the factory-built home market.

risks.title: Dependence on limited mortgage financing
risks.score_rationale: The lack of an efficient secondary market for factory-built home loans is cited as a structural barrier to growth. This risk is mentioned repeatedly with concerned language, indicating a major strategic constraint.

risks.title: Payment obligations despite customer defaults
risks.score_rationale: For loans serviced for Ginnie Mae and Freddie Mac, the company must pay principal and interest even if borrowers default. This risk is existential in the event of a wave of defaults, with technical language and no downplaying.

risks.title: Labor and material shortages
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned in forward-looking factors under MD&A, this risk affects production and costs. The language is recurring and tied to persistent macroeconomic conditions, reinforcing its relevance.

risks.title: Exposure to climate-related catastrophes
risks.score_rationale: The subsidiary insurer is exposed to storm and hurricane-related claims in Texas. Although reinsurance is in place, the risk is real and geographically concentrated, with language indicating ongoing vigilance.

ai_positioning.summary: Cavco Industries does not mention any initiatives related to artificial intelligence in its financial or operational documents. The company focuses on factory-built home production, mortgage financing, and insurance, with no reference to AI as a strategic lever.
